Let \(u,v\) be an orthonormal basis of \(L\), and write

\[
p_{ij}=u_i v_j-u_j v_i \qquad (1\le i<j\le 4).
\]

Then

\[
A_{ij}=|p_{ij}|.
\]

The Plucker coordinates of \(L^\perp\) are the Hodge-dual complementary coordinates, so

\[
B_{12}=|p_{34}|,\quad B_{13}=|p_{24}|,\quad B_{14}=|p_{23}|,
\]

and similarly for the complementary pairs. Hence the desired product is

\[
\Bigl((|p_{12}|+|p_{34}|)(|p_{13}|+|p_{24}|)(|p_{14}|+|p_{23}|)\Bigr)^2.
\]

The \(p_{ij}\) satisfy

\[
\sum_{i<j}p_{ij}^2=1
\]

and the Plucker relation

\[
p_{12}p_{34}-p_{13}p_{24}+p_{14}p_{23}=0.
\]

Define

\[
r=\frac1{\sqrt2}(p_{12}+p_{34},\,p_{13}-p_{24},\,p_{14}+p_{23}),
\]

\[
s=\frac1{\sqrt2}(p_{12}-p_{34},\,p_{13}+p_{24},\,p_{14}-p_{23}).
\]

Using the Plucker relation,

\[
|r|^2=|s|^2=\frac12.
\]

Let \(R=\sqrt2 r\) and \(S=\sqrt2 s\). Then \(R,S\in\mathbb R^3\) are unit vectors. Also, using

\[
|a+b|+|a-b|=2\max(|a|,|b|),
\]

we get

\[
|p_{12}|+|p_{34}|=\max(|R_1|,|S_1|),
\]

\[
|p_{13}|+|p_{24}|=\max(|R_2|,|S_2|),
\]

\[
|p_{14}|+|p_{23}|=\max(|R_3|,|S_3|).
\]

So it remains to maximize

\[
M_1M_2M_3,
\qquad
M_k=\max(|R_k|,|S_k|),
\]

for two unit vectors \(R,S\in\mathbb R^3\).

Reorder so \(M_1\ge M_2\ge M_3\). Since \(M_k\le1\), and among the three coordinate maxima at least two are attained by the same one of \(R,S\), we have

\[
M_2^2+M_3^2\le 1.
\]

Therefore

\[
M_1M_2M_3\le M_2M_3
\le \frac{M_2^2+M_3^2}{2}
\le \frac12.
\]

Thus the original product is at most

\[
\left(\frac12\right)^2=\frac14.
\]

Equality is attainable, for example with

\[
(p_{12},p_{34},p_{13},p_{24},p_{14},p_{23})
=
\left(\frac12,-\frac12,\frac1{2\sqrt2},-\frac1{2\sqrt2},\frac1{2\sqrt2},\frac1{2\sqrt2}\right),
\]

which satisfies the norm and Plucker relations. Then

\[
|p_{12}|+|p_{34}|=1,\qquad
|p_{13}|+|p_{24}|=\frac1{\sqrt2},\qquad
|p_{14}|+|p_{23}|=\frac1{\sqrt2}.
\]

Hence the maximum possible value is

\[
\boxed{\frac14}.
\]
